page: Microsoft Azure M64bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated mathematical and AI workloads. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external premium block storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the M64bs_v3 demonstrates strong performance characteristics across compute and memory subsystems. The single-core Geekbench score of 2174.0 places it in the top tier, while its multi-core Geekbench score reaches 19615.0. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 4509.44 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 216.83 GB/sec. Database and transactional capabilities are highlighted by a Passmark database operations score of 29566.23 and a Redis SET throughput of 71.51 million operations per second. For specialized tasks, the server achieves 26.49 tokens per second for prompt processing on a large 70B LLM, though text generation on the same model drops to an average tier of 3.35 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M64bs_v3 offers a balanced profile for enterprise workloads requiring high memory density without the overhead of local NVMe drives. By decoupling storage and utilizing premium block storage, resources are allocated efficiently toward compute and RAM. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including medium-sized relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, enterprise software compilation, and vector-based data processing.
